extracted_data.document_summary: This study performed a comprehensive fine-mapping analysis of 150 breast cancer risk regions using dense genotype data from over 217,000 subjects (109,900 breast cancer cases, 88,937 controls of European ancestry). It identified 352 independent risk signals, containing 13,367 credible causal variants (CCVs), with 191-205 high-confidence signals and 191 likely target genes. The investigation revealed that CCVs were significantly over-represented in active gene regulatory regions, open chromatin, actively transcribed genes, and transcription factor binding sites. The study also found signals differentially associated with ER-positive and ER-negative breast cancer, and prioritized target genes through integrated computational approaches like PAINTOR and INQUISIT, collectively explaining up to 23.6% of the familial relative risk. Furthermore, it included eQTL analyses in normal and tumor breast tissue to link genetic variants with gene expression changes, and explored the enrichment of CCVs with various genomic features and their impact on specific biological pathways.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Genetic fine-mapping, risk profiling, and functional genomics analysis.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This study is a genetic association and fine-mapping analysis, not an interventional therapy. It utilized dense genotype data from over 217,000 subjects (109,900 breast cancer cases, 88,937 controls) of European ancestry, analyzing over 639,000 genetic variants (SNPs, deletion/insertions, CNVs with MAF ">= 0.1% or 0.005%") across 150-152 previously defined risk regions. Methodologies included stepwise multinomial logistic regression, Bayesian approaches (PAINTOR), and a gene prioritization pipeline (INQUSIT). Statistical thresholds like conditional p-values (< 10^-6 for strong evidence, < 10^-4 for moderate) and False Discovery Rate (FDR 5%) were applied. eQTL analyses involved linear regression with specific covariates, and functional characterization included enrichment analysis with histone marks and TFBS motifs (FIMO p-value threshold 10^-3). No dose-response comparisons for a therapeutic intervention were reported.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Genetic Variants (SNPs, Credible Causal Variants (CCVs), High Posterior Probability Variants (HPPVs))
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Genomic DNA (from participant samples, inferred from genotyping arrays, breast tissue for eQTL, ER-positive breast cancer cell lines, normal breast cells)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Genetic variant identification, association, functional annotation, allele frequency, genotype measurement, eQTL identification.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Associated with higher breast cancer risk; Over-represented; Overlapped; Identified
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 352 independent risk signals, 13,367 CCVs identified across 150 regions, explaining up to 23.6% of familial relative risk. 191-205 likely target genes identified. Potentially causal variants significantly over-represented in active gene regulatory regions and transcription factor binding sites (FDR 5%). Per-allele Odds Ratios (OR) were estimated. 7 variants with HPP ">= 80%" for overall breast cancer, 10 for ER-positive, and 15 HPPVs across 13 regions. 16 additional variants with PP ">= 30%" overlapped credible eVariants. CCVs significantly overlapped eVariants in normal breast tissue (OR=2.70, p=1.7x10^-5) and tumor tissue (OR=2.34, p=2.6x10^-4).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Genetic predisposition to breast cancer, influencing gene regulation, transcription factor binding, gene expression, DNA repair, cell cycle checkpoints, and telomere maintenance.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Fine-mapping of breast cancer susceptibility regions in a large cohort (over 217,000 subjects), functional characterization of variants across different ER statuses (ER-positive, ER-negative, ER-neutral), eQTL analysis in normal and tumor breast tissue, and association studies for BRCA1 mutation carriers.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Identifies genetic loci associated with increased breast cancer risk, contributing to familial relative risk, and highlights functionally relevant variants underlying disease risk. Predicts specific risks for ER-positive and ER-negative subtypes.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Specific Deleterious/Functional Genetic Variants (rs11571833 in BRCA2, rs555607708 and rs17879961 in CHEK2, rs10069690 in TERT, rs16991615 in MCM8, rs7153397 in CCDC88C)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Genomic DNA from breast cancer associated regions
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Genetic variant identification, protein-coding sequence prediction, functional consequence analysis

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Predicted to affect; Results in truncated protein, decreased telomerase activity, telomere shortening, and increased DNA damage response.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Four coding changes previously recognized as deleterious, including stop-gain rs11571833 (BRCA2 NP_000050.2:p.K3326*), frameshift rs555607708 (CHEK2), and missense rs17879961 (CHEK2). TERT splicing variant rs10069690 results in the truncated protein INS1b.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: DNA repair, cell cycle checkpoint, DNA replication, telomere maintenance, and general cellular processes; directly alter protein function or expression.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Causal variant identification at breast cancer risk signals, breast cancer susceptibility.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Identifies specific genetic variants that directly contribute to breast cancer risk by altering critical gene functions.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Active Gene Regulatory Regions & Chromatin Features (Open Chromatin, Distal Gene Regulatory Elements, Active Promoters, H3K4me1 histone modification)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Genomic DNA (inferred from in silico analysis of genomic features), ER-positive breast cancer cell lines (MCF-7, T-47D), normal breast cells, 15 breast cell lines, eight normal human breast tissues, 111 general tissues.
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Genomic feature annotation, enrichment/overlap analysis (DNase-seq, FAIRE-seq, ChIP-Seq)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Potentially causal variants significantly over-represented (FDR 5%) in active gene regulatory regions. Significant enrichment of CCVs in open chromatin. CCVs significantly overlapped distal gene regulatory elements, with enrichment larger for ER-positive CCVs (73% of active enhancer regions overlapped by ER-positive CCVs in MCF-7 cells were inactive in normal HMEC). Significant enrichment of CCVs in active promoters in ER-positive cells (weaker evidence than for distal elements). 107 MCF-7 H3K4me1 genomic regions overlapped by ER-positive CCVs.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Control gene expression, regulate cellular processes by influencing transcription, make genes accessible for transcription factors, regulate gene expression from a distance.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Functional annotation of breast cancer risk variants, association with ER-positive breast cancer cells and normal breast.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Signifies the functional importance of these regions in mediating breast cancer risk variants' effects and elucidates mechanisms of disease-specific gene dysregulation.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Transcription Factor Binding Sites (TFBS) and TF Activity (NF-kB activity)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Genomic DNA (inferred from in silico analysis of genomic features, ChIP-Seq data), breast cancer cells (ER-negative vs. ER-positive)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Genomic feature annotation, enrichment analysis, predicted change in binding affinity, protein activity level (cited)

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Higher representation/enrichment; Predicted to modify; Higher
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Potentially causal variants significantly over-represented in TFBS. Significant enrichment of CCVs in binding sites for 40 TFs; stronger for ER-positive CCVs (ESR1, FOXA1, GATA3). 57 ER-positive signals (86%) had at least one CCV predicted to modify TFBS binding affinity (">= 2-fold"), with 48 (73%) showing ">10-fold" modification. High levels of NF-kB activity in ER-negative cells.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Mediate gene transcription, regulate gene expression by binding transcription factors, influence gene regulation through modified binding affinity, mediates inflammation and immune response.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Functional annotation of breast cancer risk variants, association with various ER-subtypes of breast cancer, ER-positive breast cancer signals, ER-negative breast cancer, inflammation and tumorigenesis.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Highlights the role of transcriptional regulation in breast cancer risk mechanisms and provides functional validation that CCVs can impact TF binding, potentially driving gene expression changes relevant to breast cancer. NF-kB activity is associated with ER-negative breast cancer phenotype.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Gene Expression Levels (eQTLs) and Actively Transcribed Genes
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Unspecified tissue/cell type (derived from existing eQTL databases, TCGA, METABRIC, NHS studies), normal breast tissue, breast tumors
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Quantitative trait locus (QTL) analysis, gene expression level measurement, genetic variant association, enrichment analysis

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Integrated into analysis; Associated with genetic variants; Higher enrichment
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Data on gene expression (eQTL) and chromatin interaction integrated into INQUSIT pipeline. Association evaluated by linear regression. Significant enrichment (FDR 5%) of CCVs in actively transcribed genes; enrichment larger for ER-neutral CCVs. eQTL variants identified with p-value threshold "\u2264 5\u00d710-4" for index variants.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Links genetic variants to changes in gene transcript levels, influencing protein synthesis and cellular function; central to cellular function and disease development.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Prioritization of genes targeted by potentially causal breast cancer variants, eQTL analysis in normal breast tissue and breast tumors, association with normal breast and ER-positive cell lines, linking genetic variants to gene activity.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Essential for identifying target genes affected by genetic variation, elucidating functional pathways related to breast cancer, and implying CCVs may impact gene transcription, contributing to susceptibility or progression.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Prioritized Target Genes and Pathways (Cancer driver genes, Transcription Factor (TF) genes, Genes targeted by multiple independent signals, Gene Ontology terms and Pathways)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Inferred from in silico analysis, existing genomic databases, predicted target genes from genomic regions (breast tissue context), high-confidence target protein-coding genes.
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Gene prioritization, functional identification, enrichment analysis, pathway enrichment analysis, statistical analysis, gene classification

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Identified and prioritized; Higher representation/enriched/classified; More genes targeted
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Known cancer drivers and TFs prioritized. Cancer driver genes over-represented among high-confidence targets (5-fold from CCVs, 15-fold from HPPVs; p=1x10^-6). 13 specific driver genes (ATAD2, CASP8, CCND1, CHEK2, ESR1, FGFR2, GATA3, MAP3K1, MYC, SETBP1, TBX3, XBP1, ZFP36L1) predicted. TF genes enriched (2-fold from CCVs, 2.5-fold from HPPVs). 165 genes targeted by multiple independent signals (p=4.3x10^-8). 20 genes prioritized via coding/splicing, 10 via promoters, 180 via distal regulatory variants. 488 Gene Ontology terms and 307 pathways identified (FDR 5%), grouped into 98 themes.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Fundamental roles in cellular growth, differentiation, regulation, DNA maintenance, immune response, cell death regulation, cell signaling, carcinogenesis; collectively impacted by genetic variants.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Application of INQUSIT pipeline for breast cancer risk variants, pathway analysis on high-confidence target protein-coding genes, ER-positive, ER-neutral, and ER-negative breast cancer etiology.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Identifies key genes whose dysregulation is central to breast cancer development and progression, elucidating functional pathways and suggesting critical hubs in breast cancer biology. Provides insights into overarching biological mechanisms perturbed by genetic risk factors, with subtype-specific pathway implications.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: ER-positive target genes/pathways (Developmental process, Immune system, Nuclear receptors)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: High-confidence target protein-coding genes (breast tissue context)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 23% (14/60) of ER-positive target genes classified in developmental process pathways; 18% in immune system; 17% in nuclear receptors pathways. Many likely causal variants overlap binding sites for transcription factor proteins (n=40 from ChIP-Seq) and co-regulators (n=64).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Gene regulation, mammary development, immune response, steroid hormone signaling, cancer driver functions (CREBBP, EP300, ESR1, GATA3, MYC).
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: ER-positive breast cancer risk, gene-regulatory regions active in ER-positive breast cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Implicated in the molecular mechanisms underlying ER-positive breast cancer susceptibility and carcinogenesis.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: ER-neutral target genes/pathways (Developmental process, Immune system, Apoptotic process)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: High-confidence target protein-coding genes (breast tissue context)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 21% (18/87) of ER-neutral target genes classified in developmental process pathways; 19% in immune system pathways; 18% in apoptotic process. ER-neutral CCVs overlapped with eVariants in normal tissue more frequently (OR = 3.51, p-value = 1.3x10^-5) than ER-positive and ER-negative CCVs.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cell development, immune response, programmed cell death.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Implicated in the molecular mechanisms underlying ER-neutral breast cancer susceptibility, suggesting distinct mechanisms of gene expression modulation.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: ER-negative target genes/pathways (DNA integrity checkpoint, Immune system, Apoptotic processes, TRAIL signaling, AP-2 transcription factors, I B kinase/NF- B signaling, cAMP, NOTCH, PI3K, RAS, WNT/Beta-catenin, FGFR, EGFR, TGFBR, DNA damage checkpoint, DNA repair, programmed cell death)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: High-confidence target protein-coding genes (breast tissue context)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: DNA integrity checkpoint and immune system each containing 19% (7/37) genes; apoptotic processes (16%). I B kinase/NF- B signaling specifically overrepresented among ER-negative target genes. 19% (25/180) of all high-confidence target genes and 19% of ER-negative target predictions are in immune system pathways. Five ER-negative high confidence target genes (ALK, CASP8, CFLAR, ESR1, TNFSF10) lie in the I- B kinase/NF- B signaling pathway.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: DNA maintenance, immune response, cell death regulation, cell signaling, carcinogenesis, inflammation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: ER-negative breast cancer risk, ER-negative breast cancer development.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Implicated in the molecular mechanisms underlying ER-negative breast cancer susceptibility and tumorigenesis. Some genes (CASP8, MDM4) have functional evidence supporting their role.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Lead variants associated with ER-positive breast cancer

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 66 signals (34%; containing 1,238 CCVs) showed the lead variant conferring a greater relative-risk of developing ER-positive tumors (false discovery rate, FDR 5%).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Genetic predisposition specifically to estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Case-only analysis for ER-positive status within strong-evidence signals of breast cancer susceptibility regions.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates genetic markers predictive of increased risk for ER-positive breast cancer subtype.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Lead variants associated with ER-negative breast cancer

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: 29 signals (15%; 646 CCVs) showed the lead variant conferring a greater risk of ER-negative cancer tumors (FDR 5%). Meta-analysis with BRCA1 mutation carriers identified 7 additional ER-negative signals, making 17% of 206 strong-evidence signals ER-negative.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Genetic predisposition specifically to estrogen receptor-negative breast cancer.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Case-only analysis for ER-negative status and meta-analysis combining BCAC ER-negative association results with BRCA1 mutation carriers from CIMBA.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates genetic markers predictive of increased risk for ER-negative breast cancer subtype.
